original.target_description: Regression of positive well-being (PWB) on social media use; discussion identifies predictor as engagement and intensity (SMEI). PWB is a composite of satisfaction with life and positive affect, not satisfaction with life alone.

n.sample_role: Participants in target regression; analytic N unresolved. The 304 usable questionnaires is a descriptive sample total, not an explicit critical-model N.
n.exclusions: Questionnaires less than 50% complete or failing a response check were not retained; model-specific missing-data exclusions are not specified.
n.location: PDF page 12 (printed p. 36), Procedures; PDF page 14 (printed p. 38), Demographics; PDF page 16 (printed p. 40), Research Question 2
n.quote:

                         F(1,422) = 7.54, p = .006 (R2 = .018, adj R2 = .015, beta = .120)

es.metric: beta (printed label; standardization not explicitly established)
es.quote:
media use significantly predicted both positive well-being with
                         F(1,422) = 7.54, p = .006 (R2 = .018, adj R2 = .015, beta = .120)

notes: Identity verified from supplied full primary-report text: title Investigating the Relationship Between Social Media Use, Big Five Personality, and Well-Being; Ulla Bunz; JoCTEC 2021 4(3), pp. 25–52; DOI 10.51548/joctec-2021-016. Text contains methods, results, discussion and references, not merely an abstract or a preregistration. No PDF was supplied, so no PDF rendering was possible. Only assigned original N and effect fields were evaluated; other fields/sides are placeholders. Same-test p = .006; R2 = .018; adj R2 = .015. Coefficient retained with literal printed beta label; no conversion or unsupported assertion of standardized beta. N=304 is not promoted to analytic N; the target regression reports F(1,422) = 7.54, which is inconsistent with the descriptive total. No N inferred from df. The target is matched to the positive-well-being result at the supplied page locator. The parenthetical life-satisfaction description is narrower than the reported PWB composite; there is no separate life-satisfaction-only coefficient in this passage. Other personality-adjusted PWB models on pages 16–18 are different tests.
